facts.statement: The genus Palaeospondylus was first described by Traquair in 1890.
Fossils of Palaeospondylus date to the Early and Middle Devonian periods.
Palaeospondylus lived approximately 400 to 390 million years ago during the Early and Middle Devonian epochs.
facts.quote: It lived during the Early and Middle Devonian epochs, around 400 to 390 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils of this genus have been found in Scotland and Australia.
facts.quote: described from fossils found in both the Achanarras slate quarry of Caithness, Scotland, and the Cravens Peak Beds of Queensland, Australia.

facts.statement: The preserved Scottish fossils indicate an eel-shaped animal up to 6 cm long.
facts.quote: indicates an eel-shaped animal up to 6 cm in length.

facts.statement: Its skull consisted of hardened cartilage and featured nasal and auditory capsules, a gill apparatus, and ambiguous jaw structures.
facts.quote: The skull, which must have consisted of hardened cartilage, exhibits pairs of nasal and auditory capsules, with a gill apparatus below its hinder part, and ambiguous indications of ordinary jaws.

facts.statement: A fossilized braincase of P. australis revealed that the animal lacked a postorbital process and an intracranial joint.
facts.quote: A fossilized braincase that belonged to P. australis showed that Palaeospondylus lacked both a postorbital process and an intracranial joint, contrary to earlier interpretations.

facts.statement: In 2004, researchers suggested that Palaeospondylus was a larval lungfish.
facts.quote: In 2004, researchers proposed that Palaeospondylus was a larval lungfish.

facts.statement: A 2017 study proposed that Palaeospondylus was a stem chondrichthyan.
facts.quote: A 2017 study suggested that it was a stem chondrichthyan.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database classifies Palaeospondylus under the class Chondrichthyes.

rejected.statement: Before 2004, the animal was classified variously as a larval tetrapod, placoderm, agnathan, stem hagfish, or chimaera.
rejected.quote: Previously, it had been classified as a larval tetrapod, unarmored placoderm, an agnathan, an early stem hagfish, and a chimaera.

rejected.statement: A 2022 study using synchrotron X-ray tomography placed Palaeospondylus phylogenetically between Eusthenopteron and Panderichthys.
rejected.quote: In 2022, researchers reported... and concluded that Palaeospondylus was between those two phylogenetically.

rejected.statement: Brownstein (2023) criticized the 2022 study, arguing instead that Palaeospondylus was a basal gnathostome.
rejected.quote: Brownstein (2023) criticized this study, suggesting it would be basal gnathostomes instead.

rejected.statement: Hirasawa and Kuratani responded to the criticism by reviewing the phylogeny and concluding the animal was closer to Acanthostega.
rejected.quote: Hirasawa and Kuratani... replied to that and reviewed phylogeny again, resulted it would be closer to Acanthostega instead.
